name: Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie NHP
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, preserves the sites of the opening and closing engagements of the Civil War. On April 12, 1861, Confederate forces fired on the Union-held Fort Sumter, beginning the four-year conflict that would cost over 600,000 American lives. Fort Moultrie, on nearby Sullivan's Island, has an even longer military history — Patriot forces there repelled a British naval attack in 1776 during the Revolutionary War in one of the first decisive American victories. The park also interprets the role of Charleston Harbor as the main port of entry for enslaved Africans brought to North America, with an estimated 40 percent of all enslaved people entering the country passing through these waters.
